BEFORE YOU PRESS REPAIR

Every byte matters.

A short guide to repairing recordings without losing sight of the original.

Start with a copy

Use a copy of the damaged recording. Keep the camera card and its folder structure intact. Reprise writes new outputs and never edits your selected original.

If your drive is failing or files are deleted, file repair alone is not the right tool. Drive recovery is a separate, planned release.

When a reference helps

An unfinished MP4, MOV, or RSV may be missing the index that explains how its audio and video fit together.

A healthy clip from the same camera and recording mode can supply missing parameters. Match codec, frame rate, resolution, and audio settings. Never record a new reference onto the affected card.

Read the result, not just the preview

A playable preview does not prove that every frame survived. Reports distinguish structural checks, full decode validation, partial salvage, and unknown completeness.

Missing or overwritten media cannot be recreated as original footage. A repair may preserve only the surviving portions.

Connect for video repair

The companion runs FFmpeg and optional reference-reconstruction tools on your computer. It requires no administrator access.

Open by default

The application source is available under GPL-3.0-or-later. Recovery and exports remain free. The project can be funded through expert assistance, studio support, and sponsored format development.

ON YOUR COMPUTER

Connect the companion

Video repair runs locally. Start the companion, then paste the pairing token it prints.

  1. Get the open-source companion

    Download the source package and follow its setup guide. FFmpeg is required for video work.

    Download source package ↗

    Mac Apple Silicon development build · Unsigned. Windows: build from source.

  2. Start it on this computer

    The companion listens only on 127.0.0.1:47831. Allow this website in your browser’s local-network prompt if asked.

  3. The token stays in this tab’s memory. It is never sent to our server.
